newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Golden Valley active on Busang hopes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Golden Valley active on Busang hopes.

text.p: Shares in Golden Valley Mines NL were at the top of the Australian share market's turnover list on Monday with more than 15 million shares traded on hopes of an imminent resolution of the development dispute over the giant Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
By 1.30 p.m. (0230 GMT), Golden Valley shares were up 1.5 Australian cents at 11.5 cents on turnover of 15.11 million shares.
Estimates suggest the deposit contains more than 57 million ounces of gold and can be mined at a cost of US$96 an ounce.

The development dispute has been mostly between Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which made the find, and Barrick Gold Corp over their respective stakes in the project along with the level of Indonesian ownership.

Other parties to the dispute now include Placer Dome and Freeport McMoran Copper and Gold Inc which both have proposals for development of Busang, and Indonesian businessman Joseph Merukh, whose company PT Krueng Gasui (KG) owns an undisputed 10 percent stake in the Muara Atan Contract of Work, which contains part of the Busang deposit.
Merukh claims another 10 percent interest through PT Sungai Atan Perdana and an option for a further 20 percent of Busang.
KG filed a C$2 billion lawsuit on January 15 in Canada against Bre-X to reinforce its claim to the deposit.
Golden Valley's exposure to the deposit is through a technical assistance and financial deal with Merukh's companies.
